official.deadline_note: The International Visegrad Fund states the call opens on 1 January 2027 at 12:00 PM with a final application deadline of 15 April 2027 at 12:00 PM and results announced 31 May 2027. Masaryk University's help page still lists an annual deadline of 15 March, which conflicts with the Fund's own timeline and should be disregarded.
official.application_cycle: 2027 call; opens 1 January 2027, closes 15 April 2027, results 31 May 2027
official.status_note: The Fund's page states the programme 'Opens on Jan 1, 2027 at 12:00 PM'; the 2026 round has closed and the next call has not yet opened.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The Fund's page states only that the amount of support is EUR 3,500 per semester for the scholar plus EUR 2,000 per semester for the host institution; it makes no statement about tuition or fees.
benefits: EUR 3,500 per semester for the scholar
EUR 2,000 per semester for the host institution
Mobility for one or two semesters at more than 190 accredited higher-education institutions across Central and Eastern Europe
Support for Master's and post-Master's students and researchers in all disciplines and in any language
No visa required for mobility between V4 states, according to Masaryk University's guidance
eligibility: Applicants must hold a bachelor's or master's degree

V4 route: citizens of Czechia, Hungary, Poland or Slovakia studying abroad at an accredited university or institute in another Visegrad country or in Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, Northern Macedonia, Serbia or Ukraine

Reverse route: Master's and post-Master's students who are citizens of Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, Northern Macedonia, Serbia and Ukraine studying in Visegrad countries
The country of the applicant's citizenship must be different from the country of the host institution
Previous levels of university studies must have been completed in a country other than the one where the scholarship is sought
Applicants may already be enrolled at the host university
The distance between the applicant's current employer/university or permanent residence and the host university should exceed 150 km
requirements: Submit the application online via My Visegrad
All uploaded documents must be written in English or accompanied by a translation certified either by a sworn translator or by a university official
Study/research period of support must be 1-2 semesters of full-time Master's level or full-time post-Master's studies/research
Preference is given to applicants not supported previously and to applicants with study/research topics relevant to the V4 region
documents: Master's level scholarship: scanned valid ID document
Master's level scholarship: scanned transcript of records covering at least the last two completed semesters, or a diploma supplement
Master's level scholarship: scanned letter of acceptance from the host university (a proof of applying is accepted if the student is not yet accepted at the time of applying)
Post-Master's level scholarship: scanned valid ID document
Post-Master's level scholarship: scanned letter of acceptance with a detailed working plan
selection_criteria: Study/research period of support must be 1-2 semesters for full-time Master's or full-time post-Master's studies/research
The country of citizenship must differ from the host institution's country and previous university studies must have been completed in another country
Preference is given to applicants not supported previously and to study/research topics relevant to the V4 region
coverage: EUR 3,500 per semester for the scholar
EUR 2,000 per semester for the host institution
Support is capped at two semesters
application_method: Find the host university or institution (the Fund's instructions cover how to find one)
Secure a letter of acceptance or proof of applying
Upload the required documents in English or with a certified translation
Submit online via My Visegrad by 15 April, 12:00 noon
Read the Visegrad Scholarship Instructions 2025 and the Visegrad Scholarship Rules PDFs published on the Fund's page
official.application_route: Submit online via My Visegrad with the required uploaded documents; the Fund publishes its own instructions and rules PDFs as the binding documents.
official.study_mode: full-time (Master's level studies or post-Master's studies/research)
official.citizenship_residency: Applicant's citizenship and residence (CZ, HU, PL, SK or EaP/WB countries) must differ from the host institution's country; previous university levels must be completed in a country other than the host country
official.international_eligibility: Yes - open in both directions, either from a V4 country to an eligible Eastern Partnership or Western Balkans country, or from those countries into the V4
official.research_requirement: For post-Master's level applicants, the letter of acceptance must be accompanied by a detailed working plan; applicant's study/research topics relevant to the V4 region are preferred
official.description: Visegrad scholarships support Master's and post-Master's students and researchers in all disciplines and in any language for up to two semesters at more than 190 accredited higher-education institutions across Central and Eastern Europe, and are financed from the International Visegrad Fund's grants, scholarships and residencies programme with the support of V4 country governments.
official.program_type: Regional government-funded mobility scholarship (International Visegrad Fund)
official.english_requirement: All uploaded documents must be written in English or accompanied by a translation certified by a sworn translator or by a university official; the study or research itself may be in any language.

travel_coverage - no travel or relocation statement is published

verification.notes: Read the International Visegrad Fund's own Apply page for the 2027 call (opens 1 January 2027, final deadline 15 April 2027) confirming EUR 3,500 per semester for the scholar plus EUR 2,000 per semester for the host institution, the 1-2 semester duration, the citizenship and distance conditions and the required documents. applicant_utility.summary: This is a mobility award for one or two semesters, not a full degree, so the first job is finding a willing host and getting a letter of acceptance or at least proof of application before the window opens on 1 January. Two conditions catch applicants out: your previous university studies must have been completed in a country other than the host country, and the host must be more than 150 km from your current university or permanent residence. Read the Fund's own Instructions 2025 and Rules PDFs, because they are the binding documents and Masaryk University's guidance on the deadline is out of date.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Master's or post-Master's students and researchers from V4 or Eastern Partnership/Western Balkans countries who want one or two semesters abroad at an accredited institution and whose topic connects to the V4 region.
application_readiness_checklist: Line up the host university and a letter of acceptance, or proof of application, before 1 January when the call opens
Verify the 150 km rule against your current university or permanent residence
Confirm your previous degree was completed in a country other than the host country
Check your transcript covers at least the last two completed semesters, or prepare a diploma supplement
Get any non-English documents translated by a sworn translator or certified by a university official
Frame the motivation around relevance to the V4 region, since that carries stated preference
common_rejection_risks: Applying to a host institution in the same country as your citizenship
Having completed your previous university studies in the same country you are applying to study in
Falling inside the 150 km radius, which the Fund states as a condition
Uploading documents not in English and not certified by a sworn translator or university official
Relaying a deadline reported by a university help page rather than the Fund's own timeline
Being a previous Visegrad scholarship recipient without a strong reason, since preference goes to applicants not supported previously
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The EUR 3,500 per semester is a flat maximum and tuition is not addressed at all, so fees, insurance, visa or migration costs and anything beyond two semesters stay on you.
document_audit: Master's level: scanned valid ID, a transcript covering at least the last two completed semesters or a diploma supplement, and a letter of acceptance or proof of applying
Post-Master's level: scanned valid ID and a letter of acceptance with a detailed working plan
Every uploaded document must be in English or carry a certification by a sworn translator or a university official - a self-made translation is not accepted
Documents must be uploaded as scans, so keep legible file sizes rather than compressed photos
alerts: The 2027 call opens 1 January at noon and the final deadline is 15 April at noon - there is no rolling benefit from applying on day one beyond avoiding a late rush
Results are announced 31 May 2027, which is tight for a September semester start
The EUR 2,000 host institution share is paid to the host, not to you
The Fund's own Instructions 2025 and Rules PDFs supersede third-party summaries, including university help pages
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Secure host acceptance or proof of application, assemble ID, transcripts and acceptance letter in English or certified, then submit everything in one online application through My Visegrad before 15 April at noon.
